newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT -JGBs seen capped, moving around 123.00.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -JGBs seen capped, moving around 123.00.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to stay under downward pressure on Wednesday after Tuesday's sharp falls.

But traders said the contract is likely to consolidate at around 123.00 as those who took fresh short positions on Tuesday may buy back, providing a solid floor around Tuesday's low of 122.81. On Tuesday, the contract closed at 123.15.
Such short-covering is highly likely to emerge on Wednesday because the next September contract is expected to take over benchmark status later this week or next week, dealers said.

"Option-linked selling from hedge funds may subside today after they finish profit-taking in futures options at least for now, their speculative sales dampened the June yesterday," said a dealer at a Japanese brokerage.
Traders said the hedge funds sold the June on Tuesday in an attempt to bring their put options with a strike price of 123.00 in the money before the expiry at the end of this week.
"But the market will remain top-heavy as sentiment will deteriorate unless operators start to consider weakness in Tokyo stocks as a bullish factor," the dealer said.

Traders said investors were likely to stay sidelined ahead of Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita's regular news conference which is scheduled to start at 3.00 p.m (0600 GMT) today. JGB futures trade finishes at 3.00 p.m.
